questions.stem:
Charlie is training for three events: a 1500 m swim, a 40 km bike ride and a 10 km run.
From past experience his times, in minutes, for each of the three events independently have the following distributions.
$S \sim \mathrm{N}(41, 5.2^2)$ represents the time for the swim
$B \sim \mathrm{N}(81, 4.2^2)$ represents the time for the bike ride
$R \sim \mathrm{N}(57, 6.6^2)$ represents the time for the run

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the probability that Charlie's total time for a randomly selected swim, bike ride and run exceeds 3 hours.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
Let $T$ = total time taken
$T \sim \mathrm{N}(41+81+57, 5.2^2+4.2^2+6.6^2)$ [So $T \sim \mathrm{N}(179, 88.24)$] M1 A1
$\mathrm{P}(T>180) = \mathrm{P}\left(Z>\frac{180-179}{\sqrt{88.24}}\right)$ M1
$= 1-0.5438 = 0.4562$ (calculator gives 0.4576…) awrt 0.456 to 0.458 M1 A1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 for setting up a normal distribution with a mean 41 + 81 + 57 (= 179)
- A1 for a correct expression of variance implied by (variance =) 88.24 or for s.d. = awrt 9.39
- M1 for standardising with 180, their mean and their standard deviation
- M1 use of $1-p$ with $0.5<p<1$

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find the probability that the time for a randomly selected swim will be at least 20 minutes quicker than the time for a randomly selected run.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
Let $Y$ = difference between run and swim or Let $D = R-S-20$
$Y \sim \mathrm{N}(16, 70.6)$ or $D \sim \mathrm{N}(-4, 70.6)$ B1
$\mathrm{P}(Y>20) = \mathrm{P}\left(Z>\frac{20-16}{\sqrt{70.6}}\right)$ or $\mathrm{P}(D>0) = \mathrm{P}\left(Z>\frac{0-(-4)}{\sqrt{70.6}}\right)$ M1
$= 1-0.6844 = 0.3156$ (calculator gives 0.3170…) awrt 0.316/0.317 M1 A1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- B1 For $\mathrm{N}(\pm 16, 70.6)$ or $\mathrm{N}(\pm 4, 70.6)$ May be seen in a calculation
- M1 for standardisation with $\pm 20$ or 0, their mean and their s.d.(their var must be > 0) must be compatible e.g. – 20 with –16
- M1 use of $1-p$ with $0.5<p<1$

parts.label: c
parts.text:
Given that $\mathrm{P}(S+B+R>t) = 0.95$
(c) find the value of $t$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
$\mathrm{P}(T>t) = 0.95 \Rightarrow \mathrm{P}\left(Z>\frac{t-179}{\sqrt{88.24}}\right) = 0.95 \Rightarrow \frac{t-179}{\sqrt{88.24}} = -1.6449$ M1 B1
$t = 163.548…$ awrt 164 A1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 for standardising using their mean and standard deviation = $z$ value $1<|z|<2$
- B1 for correct $z$ value $\pm 1.6449$ or better. Must have compatible sign with standardisation

parts.label: d
parts.text:
A triathlon consists of a 1500 m swim, immediately followed by a 40 km bike ride, immediately followed by a 10 km run.
Charlie uses the answer to part (a) to find the probability that, in 6 successive independent triathlons, his time will exceed 3 hours on at least one occasion.
(d) Find the answer Charlie should obtain.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
Let $X$ = the number of times greater than 3 hours in 6 attempts
$X \sim \mathrm{B}(6,\text{"}0.456\text{"})$ B1ft
$\mathrm{P}(X \geqslant 1) = 1-\mathrm{P}(X=0) = 1-\text{"}0.5438\text{"}^6$ M1
$= 0.9741…$ (using the calculator value gives 0.9745…) awrt 0.974/0.975 A1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- B1ft for writing or using B(6,'0.4562') ft their answer to part (a) to 3sf
- M1 use of $\mathrm{P}(X\geqslant 1)=1-\mathrm{P}(X=0)$ $[=1-(1-their(a))^6]$ allow $\mathrm{P}(X\geqslant 1)=\mathrm{P}(X=1)+\mathrm{P}(X=2)+...+\mathrm{P}(X=6)$

parts.label: e
parts.text:
Jane says that Charlie should not have used the answer to part (a) for the calculation in part (d).
(e) Explain whether or not Jane is correct.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
eg The times for each event are not now likely to be independent M1
Jane is correct / calculation is not valid A1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 Reference to the events no longer being independent (he might get tired after each event or events now follow consecutively)/ calculation does not include time between events
- A1 Correct conclusion (Jane is correct) with corresponding reason

parts.label: b
parts.technique: confidence interval for mean, known variance
parts.reason: No statement in S1-S5 covers confidence intervals; this concept (and z-interval for a mean) is not mentioned anywhere in the statements, so it is out of spec.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: probability using confidence interval result and normal distribution
parts.reason: This part depends directly on the answer to part (b) which is out of spec (confidence interval), and confidence intervals are not covered by any statement.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: hypothesis test for difference of two means using CLT/sampling distribution of sample mean
parts.reason: This requires the sampling distribution of the sample mean (CLT) for two samples, which is not covered by S5.3 (only tests for mean of a single Normal distribution) and explicitly S5.3 excludes CLT knowledge; two-sample tests are not mentioned anywhere.

parts.label: b
parts.reason: S5.3 explicitly excludes 'Knowledge of the Central Limit Theorem or other large sample approximations is not required', so any question on CLT significance is out.

parts.reason: Depends on part (d)'s Spearman's coefficient, which is not covered by any statement (only PMCC is named); Spearman's is out of spec.
